title: Prod Onboarding Risk Compact and Audit Shipping Protocol
content:
Purpose and scope:
This compact defines a minimal, auditable security acceptance pathway for moving a service or feature into production. It combines: (1) a lightweight risk acceptance "compact" (a short, evidence-focused signoff), (2) an 'audit shipping' protocol to ensure necessary events and artifacts are emitted to the SIEM and evidence store, and (3) the RBAC v2 mapping required for safe go-live. Use this doc when a team requests production onboarding or a major traffic-facing rollout.

Why a compact?
- Many releases stall on lengthy evidence packs. The compact is designed to capture the most common high-risk checks in a single page and accelerate deterministic approvals.
- It is intentionally conservative: any unresolved high-severity item must be elevated to the Security Review Board.

High-level acceptance criteria (one-line checks)
1) Access control: RBAC v2 roles assigned for deployment engineers, on-call, and observability with least privilege principle documented and linked.
2) Audit readiness: All production-facing endpoints emit structured audit events per the Audit Shipping Schema (section below) and are accepted by SIEM forwarding.
3) Evidence capture: Automated evidence collectors attached to the rollout capture configuration snapshots, IAM role bindings, and deployment manifests.
4) Fallback & degradation: Rollback or fallback path documented; automatic model/endpoint failover enabled for latency/availability SLO breaches.
5) Data controls: No PII exfiltration path; data retention and redaction rules verified.
6) Exception log: Any temporary deviations from policy recorded with owner, expiry, and compensating controls.

Risk Compact (fillable template)
- Product / Service: _______________
- Owner (engineering): _______________
- Purpose of release: quick summary (one line): _______________
- Risk Triage (High / Medium / Low): _______________
- RBAC v2 mapping attached (Y/N): __n (link) __
- SIEM acceptance test passed (Y/N): __
- Evidence automation hook created (Y/N): __
- Degradation path documented (Y/N): __
- Signed by: Security reviewer (name, timestamp): _______________
- Approval verdict: Go / Conditional Go / Blocked
- If Conditional Go, conditions and owners: 
  - Condition 1: __ owner: __ deadline: __
  - Condition 2: __ owner: __ deadline: __

RBAC v2 quick mapping guidance
- Purpose: Ensure that the minimal role set exists for release operators while preventing overbroad access to production keys and telemetry.
- Recommended roles for a typical rollout:
  - release-operator: can trigger canary/beta rollouts, view deployment logs, cannot rotate KMS or change RBAC policies.
  - site-oncall: can access runbooks, escalation tools, and toggle traffic routing; cannot modify model artifacts.
  - observability-service: write-only access for telemetry exporters and read access to dashboards.
  - incident-response: elevated temporary role (timeboxed) for post-incident mitigation.
- RBAC checklist for this release:
  1) Principle of least privilege satisfied (Y/N)
  2) Timebound elevated roles have TTL and audit hooks (Y/N)
  3) All service accounts used in deployment are listed with owners (Y/N)

Audit Shipping Protocol (practical steps)
1) Instrumentation: Integrate audit event emitter in the request path for production endpoints that perform sensitive actions (config changes, key access, privileged API calls).
2) Event schema: Emit structured events that the SIEM expects (see Audit Shipping Schema below). Use the standard library for event framing.
3) Delivery: Events must be forwarded to the centralized collector with retry and backpressure handling. If the primary stream is degraded, events must be buffered and exported within 24h.
4) Verification: Run the SIEM acceptance test (script located in linked_artifacts) which validates field presence, typing, and sampling rate. Record a test run id in the compact.
5) Retention: Confirm that raw audit events are retained per policy and that sanitized extracts are preserved for evidence export.

Audit Shipping Schema (summary for engineers)
- Requirements: Text below is an operational summary; the canonical JSON Schema is in the linked Confluence page. For quick checks ensure these fields are present and correctly typed.
  - timestamp: ISO8601 string (UTC)
  - event_id: unique string (uuid-v4)
  - actor_id: string (user/service account id)
  - actor_type: user | svc_account | role
  - action: string (e.g., deployment.trigger, key.rotate, model.load)
  - resource_type: string (e.g., endpoint, model, kms-key, secret)
  - resource_id: string (path or unique id)
  - outcome: success | failure | partial
  - request_id: correlation id linking to tracing system
  - trace_span: tracer id (optional)
  - ip_address: source IP (if applicable)
  - metadata: freeform map (string->string) with small payloads only

Notes on SIEM mapping and alerts
- Map 'action' values to normalized SIEM categories for alerting rules. Example mapping: deployment.* -> change-management.alert, key.* -> key-rotation.alert, model.* -> model-ops.alert.
- Alert on: unauthorized RBAC changes, export of >10k tokens to external sinks in 1h, repeated failed privileged actions (>5 in 10m).

Automating evidence capture
- Hooks to create at release time:
  1) Snapshot of RBAC bindings (CSV) and attached owner list
  2) Deployment manifest snapshot (git sha, image uri, model-version tag)
  3) KMS access audit sample for the last 24h (hashed principals only)
  4) SIEM acceptance test run log id and exported sample events
  5) Configuration diff vs last production deploy (if available)
- Implementation guidance: use the evidence-collector lambda (ops repo) or the release pipeline plugin. Store artifacts in the evidence bucket with retention and immutability flags.

Exception approvals (fast-path rules)
- Definition: A temporary deviation that is limited in scope and duration and has compensating controls.
- Minimum required fields for an exception: title, owner, justification, compensating control, expiry (date/time), security approver, mitigation verification plan.
- Rapid approval flow (for low-risk exceptions): Product owner files the compact entry and tags security@redwood.ai; security has 24h to review. If no response in 24h, escalate to security lead on-call.

Sign-off protocol and evidence checklist (final step)
- Before final 'Go' the following artifacts must be present and linked in the compact:
  - RBAC snapshot link (bucket or git): __
  - Audit shipping acceptance test id: __
  - Evidence collector export link: __
  - SIEM ingestion confirmation (tag or ticket): __
  - Risk Compact filled and signed: __
- Sign-off signatories:
  - Engineering owner (name + date): __
  - Security reviewer (name + date): __
  - Product owner (name + date): __

Operational playnotes (quick reminders)
- If SIEM ingestion fails during canary, abort canary and open a security incident ticket.
- For timeboxed elevated roles, confirm TTL revocation within 1 hour of expiry.
- For private deployments, ensure evidence exports to customer KMS-protected buckets are configured.

Appendix: Example audit event (text example, do not embed as canonical schema)

  "outcome":"success",
  "request_id":"req-7890",
  "ip_address":"10.2.4.5",
  "metadata":"{\"git_sha\":\"abc123\",\"canary\":\"true\"}"
}

FAQ and troubleshooting
- Q: What if evidence collector failed to produce a snapshot?
  A: Block unless security approves a targeted manual snapshot and documents the gap as an exception with compensating controls.
- Q: Who owns SIEM acceptance test fixes?
  A: Observability team owns the test harness; service team owns instrumentation fixes. Record the JIRA ticket in the compact.

Versioning and governance
- This compact is a living artifact. Major changes (policy updates, new mandatory fields in audit schema) require Security Council approval.
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any security incident that involves release control failures.

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: security@redwood.ai
- On-call security lead: pager (see internal roster)
- Observability contact: observability@redwood.ai
